content.title: About
content.content: Dark chocolate candy (NFS, item 5088) are small sweets coated with chocolate that contains a high cocoa content (usually 70 % or more). They have an intense, slightly bitter flavor typical of dark chocolate and may include additions such as nuts, dried fruit, or spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dark chocolate contains more antioxidants than milk chocolate due to its higher cocoa solids.
Demand for "pure" dark chocolate with minimal additives grew by over 15 % in Europe during the 2020s.
High‑cocoa candies are often used in pastry making to impart a deep chocolate aroma.
Dark chocolate generally has a longer shelf life than milk chocolate when stored properly.

items.title: Rich in flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids in dark chocolate act as antioxidants, supporting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium helps maintain normal muscle and nerve function and supports energy metabolism.

items.title: Mood support
items.content: Dark chocolate stimulates the production of serotonin and endorphins, which can improve mood.

items.title: Lower sugar content
items.content: Candies with a high cocoa percentage usually contain less sugar than milk‑based counterparts.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Cocoa solids provide non‑heme iron, beneficial for individuals with iron deficiency.

items.title: Cocoa allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cocoa components.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Dark chocolate is calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Dark chocolate contains modest amounts of caffeine and theobromine, which can affect sleep if consumed in large quantities.

items.title: Heavy metal residues
items.content: Poor‑quality cocoa may contain trace amounts of lead or cadmium; choose reputable brands.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dark chocolate candies can be enjoyed on their own, added to baked goods, sprinkled over ice cream, or used to make sauces for meat dishes. Let them sit at room temperature briefly to release their full aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the candies in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place (15‑18 °C). For long‑term storage, keep them in the refrigerator, but allow them to reach room temperature before eating to avoid condensation.
